Stated Claim / Post Context:
Liberals announce plans for teen prison bootcamp for young offenders

Dhurringile Prison in north-east Victoria, which has been lying dormant since its closure two years ago, will be reopened to house a program to rehabilitate young offenders under a new Liberal election plan.

Topic:Prisons

The facade of Dhurringile mansion in northern Victoria, located on the prison property. (Supplied: Hugh McGowan)

Victorian Liberal leader Jess Wilson has announced a plan to allow courts to send young offenders to the former Dhurringile Prison for a new bootcamp program if the Coalition wins November's state election.

The program would include daily physical tasks such as farm work or cleaning.

The site closed in September 2024, but local environmental and Aboriginal organisations were negotiating a purchase before the election.

The Victorian opposition says it will send young offenders to a bootcamp program near Shepparton if elected in November.

Under the Coalition plan, courts could send offenders aged between 14 and 17 to the program as an alternative to a community corrections order or other custodial sentence.

The former Dhurringile Prison near Murchison would serve as a base for the program, where those sentenced would undertake daily tasks including farm work, cleaning, maintenance, cooking and education.

Unlike existing youth justice custodial orders, young offenders sent to the bootcamp would be required to take part in the daily program.

Political parties are laying out their visions for the state's future, as voters prepare to head to the polls on November 28.

Opposition Leader Jess Wilson announced the new bootcamp program at the Coalition's campaign launch today and criticised Labor for having no plans for the facility.

"This is about instilling the discipline and respect that so many young offenders have not learned throughout their life, and crucially, giving them the skills they need to get on the right path," she said.

Jess Wilson made the announcement of the new bootcamp at her party's election launch on Sunday. (ABC News)

Nationals candidate for Shepparton Shane Sali said the program would benefit the local community.

"Bringing new activity to the facility will create opportunities for the local area, while helping address an issue that is affecting families, businesses and communities right across the Goulburn Valley," he said.

The program would be based on Queensland's Circuit Breaker program, which critics of that program say could put youth at risk of harm or abuse.
